findings.issue_text: [High/bug] packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:145-152 — The EventManager is constructed from the requesting user (`...user`, `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)`) instead of the booking's organizer; the query at lines 35-39 fetches `booking.user` with `credentials` but they are never used, so any non-organizer caller runs `updateCalendarAttendees` against the organizer's calendar event with the wrong user's credentials — the calendar event won't be updated (or errors out after the DB write).

[Medium/bug] packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:46-48 — `isTeamAdminOrOwner` joins `isTeamAdmin` and `isTeamOwner` with `&&`, requiring a user to be both simultaneously; per the variable name/intent it should be `||`, so plain team admins (and possibly owners, if the role checks are exclusive) are incorrectly denied.

[Medium/security] packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:63-71 — Guest emails are never normalized to lowercase before `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` (the blacklist itself is lowercased), so `BLOCKED@Example.com` bypasses `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS`; the same case-sensitive `guest === attendee.email` comparison also lets case-variant duplicates through.

[Medium/data] packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts:3-6 — The server schema omits the uniqueness refinement that the client enforces in `AddGuestsDialog`, and the handler's filter only compares against pre-existing attendees, so duplicate emails within a single request (e.g., via direct API call) both pass the filter and `createMany` inserts duplicate `BookingAttendee` rows.

[Medium/concurrency] packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:67-93 — The attendee-existence check and `createMany` are a non-atomic read-then-write (no transaction, upsert, or unique-constraint guard), so two concurrent `addGuests` calls for the same booking can both pass the check and insert the same guest twice.

[Medium/security] packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts:4 — `guests` has no `.max()` and the mutation has no request-level cap, so one authorized call can submit thousands of emails, each triggering an email with booking details/ICS/video links plus unbounded `BookingAttendee` inserts — an email-bombing/abuse vector.

[Low/bug] packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:154-158 — `catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }` discards `err` entirely and swallows the failure; the mutation still returns success and the UI shows "Guests added" even when notification emails failed, and the failure is undiagnosable in logs.

[Low/bug] packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:155 — `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` receives the raw input instead of the deduplicated `uniqueGuests`, so emails that were filtered out (already attendees or blacklisted) are still treated as new guests, and an existing attendee gets re-sent a full booking-confirmation email instead of the guests-added notice.

[Low/bug] packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts — There is no check of `booking.status` (or start/end time), so guests can be added to cancelled, rejected, or past bookings, generating CONFIRMED ICS REQUESTs and calendar updates for dead events.

[Low/bug] apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx:36-77 — `isInvalidEmail` is never cleared when the user edits the email inputs and isn't even reset on successful submit (only Cancel resets it), so the "Emails must be unique and valid" banner persists while correcting input and reappears when the dialog is reopened.
[Low/bug] packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx:48 — The "Remove email" tooltip is hardcoded English while the rest of the component uses `t()`, so it won't be localized.

[Medium/test_gap] No tests were added anywhere in this PR — the new `addGuests` mutation (permission matrix including the admin/owner logic, blacklist/dedupe filtering, email routing) and the new `MultiEmail`/`AddGuestsDialog` components and email templates ship with zero coverage; the `&&`/`||` authorization bug is exactly the kind of regression tests would have caught.

[Low/doc_defect] packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:63 — The handler introduces/relies on the `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS` environment variable, but it is not declared in `.env.example` or env documentation anywhere in this change, so operators won't know the knob exists or its expected format (comma-separated).

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the DB lookup includes `booking.user` with `credentials` (and `destinationCalendar`) but those fetched credentials are never used. Instead, the code builds `EventManager` from the requesting session user (`...user`) and `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)`, then calls `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)`. Since the handler explicitly allows non-organizer callers (`isAttendee` or team admin/owner) to add guests, this means a non-organizer can trigger a calendar update using their own credentials rather than the booking organizer’s credentials, plausibly causing the external calendar update to fail or update the wrong calendar after the DB write.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/concurrency] packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:67-93 — The attendee-existence check and `createMany` are a non-atomic read-then-write (no transaction, upsert, or unique-constraint guard), so two concurrent `addGuests` calls for the same booking can both pass the check and insert the same guest twice.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the code reads current attendees (`findFirst` with `include: { attendees: true }`), computes `uniqueGuests` by filtering against that snapshot, then performs `prisma.booking.update({ data: { attendees: { createMany: { data: guestsFullDetails }}}})` without a transaction, upsert, `skipDuplicates`, or any shown unique constraint guard. Two concurrent `addGuests` calls for the same `bookingId` can both see the same pre-state and both attempt to insert the same guest emails, leading to duplicate rows (or a unique-constraint error if one exists, which is not shown in this diff).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/security] packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts:4 — `guests` has no `.max()` and the mutation has no request-level cap, so one authorized call can submit thousands of emails, each triggering an email with booking details/ICS/video links plus unbounded `BookingAttendee` inserts — an email-bombing/abuse vector.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `addGuests` with `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` in `addGuests.schema.ts` and no `.max()`/server-side cap. The handler (`addGuests.handler.ts`) performs `createMany` inserts for all provided emails and then calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)`, which iterates over `calendarEvent.attendees` and sends an email per attendee (plus organizer/team emails). This makes a single authorized call capable of creating unbounded `BookingAttendee` rows and triggering a large volume of emails containing event/ICS/video details—an abuse/email-bombing vector verifiably enabled by the added code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:154-158 — `catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }` discards `err` entirely and swallows the failure; the mutation still returns success and the UI shows "Guests added" even when notification emails failed, and the failure is undiagnosable in logs.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` is wrapped in a `try/catch` that only does `console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails")` and ignores `err`, so the actual failure reason is not logged and is hard to diagnose. However, the mutation still successfully adds guests (DB update + `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees`) before sending emails, so returning success / showing “Guests added” is not necessarily incorrect behavior—only the email-notification failure is silently tolerated.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:155 — `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` receives the raw input instead of the deduplicated `uniqueGuests`, so emails that were filtered out (already attendees or blacklisted) are still treated as new guests, and an existing attendee gets re-sent a full booking-confirmation email instead of the guests-added notice.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, guests are filtered into `uniqueGuests` (excluding existing attendees and blacklisted emails) and only `uniqueGuests` are added to the booking. However, the handler calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` with the raw input `guests` instead of `uniqueGuests`. In `packages/emails/email-manager.ts`, `sendAddGuestsEmails` uses the passed `newGuests` list to decide whether to send `AttendeeScheduledEmail` vs `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail` based on `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)`. If the input includes an email that was already an attendee (thus filtered out from `uniqueGuests`), that existing attendee will still match `includes(...)` and be treated as a “new guest” for email selection, causing the wrong email type to be sent.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts — There is no check of `booking.status` (or start/end time), so guests can be added to cancelled, rejected, or past bookings, generating CONFIRMED ICS REQUESTs and calendar updates for dead events.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuestsHandler`, the booking lookup (`prisma.booking.findFirst({ where: { id: bookingId } ... })`) has no constraint/check on `booking.status` or timing (start/end). The handler will proceed to `prisma.booking.update(... attendees.createMany ...)`, `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)`, and send ICS REQUEST emails with `status: "CONFIRMED"` (see new email templates) regardless of whether the booking is cancelled/rejected/past. This can cause calendar updates and notifications for events that should be immutable/dead.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx:36-77 — `isInvalidEmail` is never cleared when the user edits the email inputs and isn't even reset on successful submit (only Cancel resets it), so the "Emails must be unique and valid" banner persists while correcting input and reappears when the dialog is reopened.

adjudication.rationale: In `AddGuestsDialog`, `isInvalidEmail` is set to `true` on validation failure (`handleAdd`), but it is only cleared in the Cancel button handler. It is not cleared on successful mutation (`onSuccess` closes the dialog and resets `multiEmailValue` but does not call `setIsInvalidEmail(false)`), nor when the user edits inputs (the `MultiEmail` `setValue` callback only updates `multiEmailValue`). Therefore the error banner can persist while correcting input and can reappear when reopening the dialog after an invalid attempt.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx:48 — The "Remove email" tooltip is hardcoded English while the rest of the component uses `t()`, so it won't be localized.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx`, the tooltip text is hardcoded as `content="Remove email"` (around the `Tooltip` wrapping the X icon), while the component otherwise uses `const { t } = useLocale()` and localizes other labels (e.g., `{t("add_another")}`). This introduces a non-localized user-facing string for non-English locales.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/test_gap] No tests were added anywhere in this PR — the new `addGuests` mutation (permission matrix including the admin/owner logic, blacklist/dedupe filtering, email routing) and the new `MultiEmail`/`AddGuestsDialog` components and email templates ship with zero coverage; the `&&`/`||` authorization bug is exactly the kind of regression tests would have caught.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds substantial new functionality (TRPC `addGuests` mutation, new dialog/UI, email templates) without any accompanying test changes visible in the PR, and it also contains a concrete authorization logic defect: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed with `&&` between `isTeamAdmin(...)` and `isTeamOwner(...)` (in `addGuests.handler.ts`), meaning only users who are *both* admin and owner pass, which is likely unintended and can incorrectly deny access. This is a real, diff-grounded correctness/security bug, and the absence of tests increases risk of such regressions.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/doc_defect] packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:63 — The handler introduces/relies on the `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS` environment variable, but it is not declared in `.env.example` or env documentation anywhere in this change, so operators won't know the knob exists or its expected format (comma-separated).

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts` the new logic reads `process.env.BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS` and expects a comma-separated list (`split(",").map(...)`). This diff does not add any corresponding entry/update to an `.env.example` file or any env documentation within the shown changes, so the new operational configuration knob is introduced without being discoverable from this PR’s diff.
